summary:
Aetheris is an interactive web platform developed by Team EON for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, addressing the Planet X and SPHEREx challenge.

Our project makes NASA's SPHEREx observations more accessible to students, educators, astronomy enthusiasts, and curious minds. Users can search for regions of the sky using right ascension, declination, and field of view, explore observations from different dates, and examine potential changes in celestial objects through an intuitive visual interface.

Aetheris combines a React-based frontend with Python and Django REST services that access real scientific data from NASA/IPAC IRSA, retrieve observation metadata, and process astronomical FITS files. The platform also includes temporal visualization and spectral exploration modules, with scientific integration continuing as the prototype evolves.

By reducing the technical barriers to accessing astronomical data, Aetheris aims to promote science education, curiosity, and citizen participation in exploring the universe.

Our vision is simple: make scientific discovery more approachable, meaningful, and accessible to everyone.
details:
Aetheris is a web platform developed by Team EON for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, addressing the Planet X and SPHEREx challenge. Our goal is to simplify the exploration of astronomical observations and make scientific data more accessible to students, educators, and astronomy enthusiasts.

The platform allows users to search for regions of the sky using Right Ascension (RA), Declination (Dec), and Field of View (FOV). Through NASA/IPAC IRSA, the backend retrieves real SPHEREx observations and processes scientific FITS files. The interface includes temporal visualization tools for comparing observations from different dates and a spectral explorer designed around SPHEREx's 102 infrared channels.

Aetheris was developed using React, TypeScript, and Vite for the frontend, alongside Python, Django REST Framework, Astropy, Astroquery, and PyVO for scientific data access and processing. Its architecture incorporates PostgreSQL, Redis, Celery, and Docker to support data management and asynchronous operations.

During development, we implemented observation queries, scientific processing services, and interactive visualization components. A documented query to the M101 region successfully retrieved 246 observation records. Integration between some frontend modules and scientific services remains in progress.

Our innovation lies in bringing temporal comparison, infrared exploration, and scientific information together in an intuitive educational experience. We aim to reduce technical barriers, encourage critical thinking, and open new opportunities for citizen science.

Aetheris transforms access to astronomical data into an opportunity to explore, learn, and investigate the universe.
